title: Jordana:
title_q: “What I Do When My Baby Is Stuffy”
headline: An experienced mom on the playroom floor counts her three stuffy-baby steps, and the third one, the BN02 nasal aspirator with its lights and music, gets Jamie breathing better and smiling.
story: Jordana sits on the floor with Jamie (21 months) and talks to camera. She gives a real three-step routine: humidifier, nasal spray, then the nasal aspirator. The aspirator is step three, not the whole video. That is the soft sell the client asked for.

Then we see it in real use: she turns it on, shows the suction setting, the changing colors and the music, and gently uses it on Jamie. Jamie stays calm and smiles. Jordana ends on what she hears: her congestion is clearing up and she is breathing better.
How it differs from Kara's tip: Kara's cut is its own story. This one is built on Jordana's three-step list and on the lights and music making it easy for a toddler.

Loops: L1 “What are the three things?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:14 (“the nasal aspirator”). L2 “Does it work on a toddler?” opens at 0:14 and closes in the BUTTON (“she's breathing better”, Jamie smiling). Stakes: a stuffy toddler who cannot breathe well.
do: Open on Jordana mid-sentence with the hook text already on screen at 0:00.
Cut away from her face often. Every product beat shows Jamie on camera.
Use the gentle use on Jamie from IMG_9443 01:12 to 01:25 as the product hero.
Keep the product mention short. Let the lights and music sell it.
End on Jamie calm or smiling, then the end card.
dont: No logo, no name card, no fade at 0:00.
No shot of Jamie pulling away or saying no (IMG_9443 01:04 to 01:10 is out).
No director voice. Atdhe's coaching lines are marked in the transcript.
Do not use IMG_9443 01:00 to 01:07 or 02:26 to 02:56. The Experienced Routine cut uses those moments.
